workflow_steps.objective: Confirm the restaurant group’s business goals, brand architecture, audiences, locations, offer, scope, constraints, success criteria, approvals and required asset list.
Study the group’s positioning, customer occasions, cultural context, competitors, venue experience and relevant category conventions without treating the published reference as a style brief.
Define the positioning, brand idea, verbal and visual principles, differentiation criteria and rules for balancing group consistency with restaurant-level flexibility.
Develop meaningfully distinct identity directions covering brand idea, naming implications, logo approach, typography, colour and graphic language.
Evaluate directions against the agreed principles and obtain an explicit client decision before further development.
Resolve feedback and test the selected direction for recognition, legibility, cultural suitability and practical use across representative contexts.
Build the approved direction into a governed system of logo variants, typography, colour, imagery, graphic elements, hierarchy, accessibility and usage rules.
Specify the content hierarchy, formats, dimensions and production requirements for priority restaurant, digital and environmental applications.
Apply the approved identity system consistently across the agreed family of brand touchpoints and restaurant-group variants.
Prepare technically valid artwork masters, templates and specifications for the agreed digital, print and environmental outputs.
Validate completeness, naming, formats, links, colour modes, fonts, licences and documentation before packaging and handing off final assets.

observations: The visible outcome uses a predominantly purple field with cream, white and muted tan linework.
A large, highly detailed guardian-lion illustration occupies the centre of a symmetrical composition.
Four vertically arranged seal-like forms flank the central figure, each combining large Chinese characters with smaller circular symbols.
Bold uppercase English typography spans the upper and lower edges, while smaller vertical text appears beside the central illustration.
The composition demonstrates an identity extended through illustration, bilingual typography, emblematic devices and a tightly controlled limited palette.
The image is low resolution and shows a flattened published outcome; it does not reveal source artwork, construction rules, production specifications or an underlying design process.

missing_inputs: Restaurant group name, existing brand equity and whether naming or renaming is in scope
Business strategy, positioning ambition, value proposition and measurable success criteria
Brand architecture, restaurant portfolio, sub-brand relationships and future expansion plans
Priority audiences, locations, languages and relevant cultural considerations
Competitor set and available customer, market or operational research
Confirmed deliverable inventory, rollout phases, channels and venue touchpoints
Venue plans, signage constraints, menu formats and supplier or fabrication requirements
Approved copy, menu content, photography or illustration needs and content ownership
Budget, schedule, review milestones, decision-makers and final approval authority
Required accessibility, trademark, licensing, regulatory and language-review standards
Existing source assets, fonts, image rights and technical production specifications
assumptions: The engagement creates or substantially renews the restaurant group identity rather than making a minor edit to an established system.
The identity must work across multiple restaurant and corporate touchpoints, but the exact application list remains subject to scoping.
Environmental applications are relevant because the client operates physical restaurant venues.
Mockups are presentation and validation artifacts unless production of final fabricated items is separately commissioned.
Packaging, ecommerce, photography and merchandise are not included unless confirmed during intake.
The supplied image is used only as evidence of the visible deliverable family and not as a stylistic direction to reproduce.
stop_conditions: Do not begin concept development until the strategic brief, scope, brand architecture, decision-makers, budget and timeline are approved.
Do not refine or systematize a direction until the client explicitly selects one concept.
Do not expand the system across the full asset family until the core identity and representative application tests are approved.
Do not prepare production masters without final copy, dimensions, venue or vendor specifications, licensed assets and required legal or language clearances.
Do not deliver until final approval is recorded and the asset package passes completeness, technical and rights checks.
Pause and re-scope if naming, packaging, photography, fabrication or additional sub-brands are introduced beyond the approved programme.
rationale: The request spans strategy, identity creation, systematic application and final handoff, so concept_to_production is the strongest available classification. The workflow introduces explicit approval gates before refinement, system expansion and production, while the reference is treated only as visible evidence of the kinds of identity elements and applications a published restaurant-brand outcome may contain.
